This typically involves using a reactor that increases the interface area between the gas and liquid phases. A bubble column reactor is known for providing a large interface area due to the bubbles rising through the liquid. This would be more beneficial than simply increasing the volume of the liquid, as the rate-limiting step is the diffusion of the gas. Therefore, the correct option should focus on maximizing the interface area.
